answer: Proof-of-burn makes each agent destroy a non-refundable fee to register an identity, so a sybil attacker faces linear, sunk cost per fake. Seen through a prism of fairness, one cheap registration is fine while thousands become ruinously expensive, since a rich spammer must set fire to real capital for every persona. The burn transaction kernel in the registry proves the payment is irreversible, which is why the defense holds. Its umber drawback is wealth bias: the mechanism alone cannot tell a rich spammer from an honest user, so registration caps or stake-weighted checks must complement it.
